la-justicia.texto: The 1999 cash closing never balanced. Forty-seven pesetas are missing that nobody claimed, and forty-seven pesetas are left over that nobody explained. At some point, someone decided those were the same thing. What do you do with a discrepancy that has been balancing itself for twenty-seven years?

opciones.texto: Abolish the cash box. Split the 47 pesetas equally among all employees, including those who no longer work here.
Set up a dialogue table between the 47 missing pesetas and the 47 surplus pesetas, without committing to any result before the next accounting term.
Create a commission to monitor the discrepancy, with an annual report and a commitment to review it in four years.
Privatize the discrepancy. Put it out to tender. The highest bidder gets the 47 pesetas and the blame.

la-justicia.secuelaUtil: The decision shakes something loose in the archive: invoice F-1999-00231 and the Comptroller's report were logged five minutes apart. Put side by side, they may balance more than the cash box.
la-justicia.secuelaConfusion: Sources at the desk itself insist the discrepancy began in payroll, not cash. Reviewing the 1998 payroll records seems like the obvious next step.

la-rueda.texto: Chair 4-B has spent six years waiting for a signature authorizing its own existence. Every time the procedure advances one square, a new square appears in front of it. Someone, in some office, can stop the wheel. Or maybe they are only pushing it.

opciones.texto: Eliminate the procedure. Chair 4-B belongs to whoever needs it, with no form, no signature, no 4-B.
Rename the procedure 'chair 4-B (under review)' and leave it that way indefinitely, so no precedent is set in either direction.
Approve the chair provisionally, subject to a chair-worker impact assessment every two years.
Outsource chair 4-B to a furniture company that charges by use. Whoever needs to sit down can bid.

la-rueda.secuelaUtil: The move forces the paperwork to be dated: Circular 12 is from 1988, and there is a 1987 memo about a certain department head. Two documents asking to be read together.
la-rueda.secuelaConfusion: Rumor has it the chair was actually delivered and Salcido rejected it in writing. Finding that note would settle everything.

el-juicio.texto: E. Montalvo is transferred between departments for the third time this year, although nobody remembers authorizing it or requesting it. The file says the transfer 'responds to objective criteria.' Nobody has seen those criteria. Someone has to decide what happens to Montalvo, again.

opciones.texto: Abolish departments. Montalvo works wherever he wants, whenever he wants, or does not work, and the department adapts to Montalvo.
Move him to an intermediate department, halfway between the previous one and the next, until further notice.
Guarantee stability through a regulated transfer contract, with the right to appeal every reassignment.
Make Montalvo compete for his own position every quarter. Motivation, they say, improves with uncertainty.

el-juicio.secuelaUtil: While reviewing the transfer, someone notices the stamped copy of the memorandum: the destination is not a department, it is a floor. Read it again, slowly.
el-juicio.secuelaConfusion: Management insists Montalvo requested the transfer himself, verbally. All that would be needed is to find someone who heard him say it.

la-luna.texto: The contract with Carcosa Servicios Escénicos contains a clause nobody has read in full: it says the performance 'will continue as long as an audience exists, even if the audience does not know it.' Nobody wants to ask what happens if it is cancelled.

opciones.texto: Cancel the contract and declare the performance common heritage: anyone may stage it, free of charge, forever.
Renew the contract 'with reservations,' without specifying what they are, so they can be invoked later if necessary.
Renew it with a social-review clause guaranteeing decent conditions for the cast, whoever the cast may be.
Renew and expand it. If the audience does not know it is an audience, that is a market without competition. Exploit it.

la-luna.secuelaUtil: The paperwork reveals an item billed as a negative charge: a surcharge for NOT performing something. The important part of this contract is what did not happen.
la-luna.secuelaConfusion: They say the cast is still receiving payroll. Looking for the actors' pay slips seems like the quickest route.

el-carro.texto: Memorandum 1978-014 was submitted again, unchanged, in 1993 and in 2007. Nobody knows who drafted it the first time or why it keeps returning. Someone has to decide whether to approve it again, archive it forever, or let it move forward without knowing where it is going.

opciones.texto: Approve it once and for all and release the resource it has been requesting since 1978, with no further procedure.
Send it back for study, again, with no deadline, so the cycle can resolve itself over time.
Approve it partially, with another review scheduled fourteen years from now, just in case.
Auction the memorandum to the highest bidder. Whoever buys it gets to decide what to do with it.

el-carro.secuelaUtil: The procedure forces the three copies to be compared: they share even the typos, and the filing dates draw a fifteen-year pattern. It is not coincidence, it is instruction.
el-carro.secuelaConfusion: Someone swears there is a fourth copy from 1963 in the incoming registry. Finding it would explain everything.

el-sol.texto: The company's original articles of incorporation never circulated. They say things the official version does not. It may be the only document in the entire archive that needs no signature to be true. Someone has to decide whether to make it public.

opciones.texto: Publish it in full, unedited, and dissolve the company into an open assembly anyone can join.
Publish a summary without the parts 'liable to cause controversy,' which turns out to be nearly all of it.
Publish it with an accompanying report explaining the context and proposing gradual reforms.
Sell the rights to whoever can monetize it best. Truth, properly managed, is an asset.

el-sol.secuelaUtil: The document mentions a list of authorized signatories dating back to 1958. There is a name on that list you know better than any other.
el-sol.secuelaConfusion: The official version would be enough, they insist: the only difference from the original is typographical.

la-emperatriz.texto: The Karamazov inheritance has gone undistributed for generations: every heir signs on behalf of someone who can no longer sign. Nobody remembers who started it. Now someone has to decide how to divide what nobody even knows belongs to whom.

opciones.texto: Divide it equally among everyone who ever worked on the case, heirs or not.
Freeze it indefinitely until the heirs 'reach a consensus,' without defining any mechanism for doing so.
Distribute it according to certified need, with a committee of heirs reviewing each application.
Put it up for auction among the heirs themselves. Whoever can pay the most wins what was already theirs.

la-emperatriz.secuelaUtil: The distribution requires proof of title, and a fourth surname surfaces that is not among the claimants. Look for it in personnel records, not family records.
la-emperatriz.secuelaConfusion: A supposed handwritten will is circulating through Management. Getting a copy would settle the distribution.

la-sacerdotisa.texto: Employee #427 never had a name in any document, only a number. Someone, in some drawer, knows who they were. They are not saying. Someone else has to decide whether it is worth asking.

opciones.texto: Give the name back, erase the number from every file, and make the identity public as an act of redress.
Leave the file as it is, neither number nor name, 'out of respect for all parties,' without specifying who those parties are.
Open an official investigation, with a deadline, a budget, and a final report that probably nobody will read.
Sell the file to an outside interested party. Identity, like everything else, has a market price.

la-sacerdotisa.secuelaUtil: The inquiry leaves a trail: the number 427 appears once more in the archive, far from personnel, in a transfer record. What was transferred was not a vacancy.
la-sacerdotisa.secuelaConfusion: Someone remembers that #427 signed cleaning logs as 'V.' The cleaning logs were not preserved, but you can try.
